escalationBullets: If the WAN IP of your own router is private, there is definitely another upstream routing layer.
If the router UI lists multiple copies of the same device, delete stale target entries before re-testing.
recommendedActions: Confirm the selected target device matches the host Mac.
Use the detected local IP from the app when possible.
Delete duplicate rules that point to old devices.
Check whether your ISP device and your own router are both doing routing.
If possible, put one device into bridge / passthrough mode.
Otherwise forward on the upstream router as well.
Check the Mac's current local IP in the app.
Update the router rule so it points to the current local IP.
Reserve the Mac's IP in the router later so it stops changing.
Confirm the selected target device is the Mac running Minecraft Server Controller.
Match the target device entry to the local IP shown in the app.
Remove duplicate rules that still point to older devices.
Check whether both the ISP device and another router or mesh system are routing.
Put one device into bridge / passthrough mode when possible.
Re-check the Mac's current local IP in Minecraft Server Controller.
Update the router rule so it points to the current host Mac address.
Reserve the Mac's DHCP address later so it stops changing.
expected.summary: Most likely cause: The port forward may point to the wrong target device. Also check: You may be behind two routers, Your Mac's local IP changed.

notes: Three causes fire at once: wrong-device (score 8, strong), double-nat (score 8, possible), local-ip-changed (score 7, strong). Confirms the full three-way sort: score descending first (7 sorts last); a tie at score 8 is broken by confidence (strong before possible), not by insertion or topic-title order.
